description: The plot illustrates how Accuracy varies as a function of s_pop frequency for two series. The x-axis is labeled “s_pop frequency (x10^4)” and uses a linear scale with tick marks at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, and 19, spanning approximately 1 to 19 (in units of ×10^4). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. One line is blue with circular markers and a dashed style, showing values around 0.70 at x=1, rising to about 0.92 at x=3 and about 0.97 at x=5, staying near 0.95–1.00 through x=11, dipping to about 0.90 at x=13, and returning to about 1.00 from x=15 through x=19; this series includes vertical error bars at each point. The other line is green with square markers and a solid style, starting near 0.36 at x=1, increasing to about 0.45 at x=3, about 0.60 at x=5, and about 0.68 at x=7, dropping to about 0.45 at x=9, rising to about 0.66 at x=11, moving to about 0.60 at x=13 and about 0.50 at x=15, then reaching about 1.00 at x=17 and remaining about 1.00 at x=19; this series also shows vertical error bars at each point.
